_comment: SAT-SA peer benchmarking configuration.
This file is the ONLY place a peer benchmark metric is declared. The
benchmarking engine contains no metric arithmetic of its own: it reads
these declarations and resolves them against values other layers have
already produced. That is what keeps a peer statement consistent with
the same quantity shown elsewhere in the assessment.
EVERY NUMBER HERE IS JUSTIFIED, NOT CHOSEN
min_peers / robust_min_peers
Minimum cohort size before a peer median is published at all, and
the size at which the cohort is described as robust. Below the
first threshold no baseline is produced, because a median of two
observations is not a distribution. Between the two thresholds
the baseline is published and explicitly labelled limited, so a
reviewer can see the difference between a weak baseline and no
baseline.
deviation bands
|modified z| at or above which a deviation is reported as
NOTABLE or MATERIAL. These are descriptive bands for choosing
wording, not supervisory policy and not control-failure
thresholds. No band creates a finding, changes a verdict, or
alters an evidence state.
PERCENTILE IS NOT A RISK SCORE
Each metric declares a direction. The direction is the only thing that
makes a percentile interpretable, and it is declared here rather than
inferred in the interface, so no screen can decide on its own that a
high number is bad.
higher_is_adverse     a larger value is the less favourable one
higher_is_favourable  a larger value is the more favourable one
A metric that expresses evidence presence rather than performance
('how much of the submitted data carried the concept this metric is
measured over') is marked measure_type 'evidence_observation'. Those
metrics are reported, compared and labelled, and the interface is
told through this field not to present them as performance.
NO NEW INTELLIGENCE
No metric introduces a judgement the supervisory layers did not reach.
Each names the existing result key it is resolved from. A value that
those layers declined to produce is reported as NOT_EVALUABLE with the
reason the underlying layer gave, never as zero and never imputed.
Cohort-size policy for publishing a peer baseline. Applied
identically to every metric and every scope.
Descriptive bands over the absolute modified Z-score. They select
wording only. They are not thresholds of failure and they never
produce or suppress a finding.

higher_is_adverse_above: {scope_label} reported {observed}, above the peer median of {peer_median}
({modified_z} reference spreads from that median across {peer_count}
peer scopes at the {percentile_ordinal} percentile of this cohort).
higher_is_adverse_below: {scope_label} reported {observed}, below the peer median of {peer_median}
({modified_z} reference spreads from that median across {peer_count}
peer scopes at the {percentile_ordinal} percentile of this cohort).
higher_is_favourable_above: {scope_label} reported {observed}, above the peer median of {peer_median}
({modified_z} reference spreads from that median across {peer_count}
peer scopes at the {percentile_ordinal} percentile of this cohort).
higher_is_favourable_below: {scope_label} reported {observed}, below the peer median of {peer_median}
({modified_z} reference spreads from that median across {peer_count}
peer scopes at the {percentile_ordinal} percentile of this cohort).
within_cohort_spread: {scope_label} reported {observed}, inside the peer median of
{peer_median} ({modified_z} reference spreads from that median across
{peer_count} peer scopes at the {percentile_ordinal} percentile of this cohort).

metrics.label: Execution gap incidence
metrics.numerator_definition: Records in the scope carrying at least one POTENTIAL_EXECUTION_GAP finding.
metric_definition: Share of records in the scope where the same submitted evidence
states an expectation and contradicts it. This is the only
measure in the catalogue derived from a contradiction the
execution-gap layer could actually establish, and it inherits
that layer's record-level traceability.
_source_concepts_comment: Declared as the concepts the configured execution-gap rules read.
A concept the scope's evidence did not resolve is reported as
unresolved in source_concepts rather than silently included.

metrics.label: Negative space incidence
metrics.numerator_definition: Records inside a triggered negative-space population that carried no usable expected evidence.
metrics.denominator_definition: Records inside a triggered negative-space population.
metric_definition: Share of the applicable population for which evidence that the
configured expectation says should exist was absent or unusable.
Only expectations whose trigger population is actually present in
the scope enter the denominator, so a scope without the trigger
population is reported as not evaluable rather than as perfect.
_source_concepts_comment: Declared as the concepts the configured negative-space rules

metrics.label: Operational pattern incidence
metrics.numerator_definition: Records in the scope appearing in at least one POTENTIAL_OPERATIONAL_ANOMALY cluster.
metric_definition: Share of records the operational-shape layer placed in a cluster
it could not explain by chance. Records outside every pattern's
population cannot be flagged, so this is an upper bound on
flagged activity within the scope rather than a complete count.
A signal here is a request for human review, not a control failure.

metrics.label: Anomalous scope
metrics.numerator_definition: Scopes the anomaly layer returned a POTENTIAL_OPERATIONAL_ANOMALY verdict for.
metric_definition: Share of evaluated scopes the anomaly model returned a potential
operational anomaly verdict for. The verdict belongs to the model
layer and its reference population; this catalogue only counts it
and reports the cohort it was counted across.

metrics.label: Capability evidence coverage
metrics.numerator_definition: Capabilities the capability layer reported AVAILABLE.
metrics.denominator_definition: Capabilities the capability layer evaluated for the scope.
metric_definition: Share of configured capabilities for which the submitted data
carried enough canonical evidence to assess. This describes the
submission, not the strength of a control: a capability reported
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE counts in the denominator, never as a failure.

metrics.label: Escalation evidence coverage
metrics.numerator_definition: Capabilities declaring ESCALATION_GAP and reported AVAILABLE.
metrics.denominator_definition: Capabilities declaring ESCALATION_GAP and evaluated for the scope.
metric_definition: Share of the capabilities whose configured indicator category is
escalation gap where enough evidence existed to assess them.
Describes evidence availability for escalation, not escalation
performance.

metrics.label: Investigation evidence coverage
metrics.numerator_definition: Capabilities declaring INVESTIGATION_QUALITY and reported AVAILABLE.
metrics.denominator_definition: Capabilities declaring INVESTIGATION_QUALITY and evaluated for the scope.
metric_definition: Share of the capabilities whose configured indicator category is
investigation quality where enough evidence existed to assess
them. This measures whether investigation evidence was submitted
at all, which is not the same as whether the investigation that
was submitted was thorough.

metrics.label: Monitoring visibility evidence coverage
metrics.numerator_definition: Capabilities declaring MONITORING_VISIBILITY_GAP and reported AVAILABLE.
metrics.denominator_definition: Capabilities declaring MONITORING_VISIBILITY_GAP and evaluated for the scope.
metric_definition: Share of the capabilities whose configured indicator category is
monitoring visibility where enough evidence existed to assess
them. Describes whether monitoring could be evidenced, not whether
monitoring was effective.

cohort_tiers.label: Same period, sector, class and size
selection_rule: Scopes resolved to the same period label as the target, and whose
evidenced sector, entity class and size band all equal the
target's evidenced values. Every attribute must be evidenced on
the target; a target missing any of them cannot enter this tier.

cohort_tiers.label: Same period, sector and class
selection_rule: Scopes resolved to the same period label as the target, and whose
evidenced sector and entity class equal the target's. Size band is
not required here, so this tier is broader than tier 1.

cohort_tiers.label: Same period
selection_rule: Scopes resolved to the same period label as the target, regardless
of sector, class or size. This is the widest cohort the tool will
build, because comparing scopes drawn from different periods would
compare different operating conditions rather than different

_comment: Sector, entity class and size band are read only from here.
There is deliberately no inference from a dataset column, a name
pattern or a default. An attribute is used for cohort selection only
when a supervisory authority has supplied it here for that entity id,
and the resulting cohort reports which attributes were actually
evidenced. A tier that needs an attribute nobody supplied reports
itself unavailable with that reason, rather than quietly widening to
a tier that looks more precise than the evidence supports.
Keys are entity ids as resolved by the assessment scope resolver.
